paper.title: Multi-Armed Bandit Based Client Scheduling for Federated Learning

settings.name_in_paper: Client scheduling in the ideal scenario (combinatorial MAB, super arm of N clients)
unmapped: Super-arm reward is the minimum (bottleneck) of the selected base-arm rewards: r(S) = 1 - max_{k in S} tau_k/tau_max
settings.definition_quote: The chosen subset of the arms $\calS(t)$ is referred to as a super arm and its corresponding normalized reward is $r(\calS(t))=-\bar{\tau}(\calS(t))+1\in[0,1)$ ... the optimal super arm is $\calS^{\ast}=\argmax_{\calS\subseteq\calK,|\calS|=N}\{\min_{k\in \calS}\mu_k\}$ ... $\Sigma^{\pi_1}=T\mu(\calS^{\ast})-\Ex[\sum_{t=1}^{T} r(\calS(t))]$

settings.name_in_paper: Client scheduling in the non-ideal scenario (availability and fairness constraints)
unmapped: Super-arm reward is the minimum of selected base-arm rewards
Set of available clients A(t) is i.i.d. over time with unknown distribution and revealed at the start of each round; exactly min{N,|A(t)|} clients must be chosen
Long-term fairness constraint liminf (1/T) sum_t E[b_k(t)] >= c_k; the learner knows the fairness vector c
Regret is measured against the optimal stationary randomized A-only policy solving the fairness-constrained LP
settings.definition_quote: Given an optimal $\calA$-policy $\pi^\ast$, we define $r^{\ast}$ as the maximal reward of problem \eqref{linear problem} ... $\Sigma^{\pi_2}=   Tr^{\ast}-\Ex\bigg[\sum_{t=1}^{T} r(\calS(t))\bigg], \ \ \text{s.t.} \ \eqref{fairness constraint} \ \text{and} \ \eqref{availability constraint3}.

settings.name_in_paper: Convergence of FL training (gradient aggregation over scheduled clients)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Convergence of federated gradient-descent training, not a bandit problem
unmapped: Stochastic gradient estimates with bounded variance or first/second moment conditions on the aggregated update
settings.definition_quote: The FL training aims to minimize the weighted global loss function ... $\min_{\qx} G(\qx)=\sum_{k\in\calK}\varpi_k G_{k}(\qx)$

symbols.Delta_max_S: max over non-optimal super arms of Delta_S = sum_{k in S*} mu_k - sum_{k in S} mu_k
symbols.Delta_min_S: min over non-optimal super arms of Delta_S = sum_{k in S*} mu_k - sum_{k in S} mu_k

tuning: exploration bonus sqrt((N+1) ln t / z_k)

source.label: upper bound theorem 1
source.quote: The expected regret achieved by the proposed CS-UCB algorithm presented in \textbf{Algorithm  \ref{alg1}} is upper bounded by \Sigma^{\pi_1}<\Delta_{\max}\left[\frac{K}{N}+1+\frac{4N^2(N+1)K\ln T}{(\Delta_{\min})^2}+K+\frac{\pi^2}{3}NK\right], where $\Delta_{\max}=\max_{r(\calS)\leq r(\calS^{\ast})} \Delta_{\calS}$,  $\Delta_{\calS}=\sum_{k\in\calS^{\ast}}\mu_k-\sum_{k\in\calS}\mu_k$, and $\Delta_{\min}=\min_{r(\calS)\leq r(\calS^{\ast})} \Delta_{\calS}$.

results.notes: Paper's N (channels = clients per super arm) mapped to m. Strict inequality. Gaps defined via linear sums of means while regret uses min-reward; proof upper bounds min-regret by sum-regret. Algorithm loop runs until T but index uses ln t; treated as anytime.

symbols.beta_w: weighting factor in [0,1] between UCB estimate and virtual queue
symbols.Omega: sum_k max{c_k^2, (1-c_k)^2}, c_k the fairness requirement of client k

conditions: fairness vector c strictly inside the maximal feasibility region

source.label: upper bound theorem 2
source.quote: The expected regret achieved by the proposed CS-UCB-Q algorithm presented in \textbf{Algorithm  \ref{alg2}} is upper bounded by \Sigma^{\pi_2}\leq  \beta\frac{\Omega T}{2}+(1-\beta)\Big[(\frac{\pi^2}{3}+1)K+4\sqrt{2KNT\ln T}\Big], where $\Omega=\sum_{k\in\calK}\max\{c_k^2,(1-c_k)^2\}$.

results.notes: N mapped to m. Comparator is the optimal A-only (stationary randomized) policy of the fairness-constrained LP. Feasibility (Theorem 3) is not a regret bound and not recorded. Proof is a sketch referring to Li et al. 2019.

conditions: fairness vector c strictly inside the maximal feasibility region

source.label: upper bound theorem 2
source.quote: Typically when $0<\beta\leq\frac{1}{\sqrt{T}}$ and $T$ is large enough, we have \Sigma^{\pi_2}\leq  \frac{\Omega \sqrt{T}}{2}+(\frac{\pi^2}{3}+1)K+4\sqrt{2KNT\ln T}.

results.notes: Tuning beta depends on T, so horizon known. N mapped to m.

conditions: Assumptions 1-4: unbiased evaluation, L-smooth, Phi-strongly convex (alpha=Phi), bounded gradient variance
